blocks.text: A function is a block of code that performs a specific task and can be reused whenever needed.

items: Avoids writing the same code again and again.
Makes programs simple and easy to understand by breaking into smaller parts.
Finding and fixing errors become easier.
blocks.heading: Functions in programming

items: These predefined functions provided by programming languages or libraries to perform common tasks such as mathematical calculations, input/output, or string operations.
For example, the sqrt() function from the C++ <cmath> library calculates the square root of a number.
blocks.heading: Built-in functions
Built-in functions

items: These functions are functions written by programmers to perform specific tasks required in a program.
They help organize code and allow reuse of logic whenever needed.

blocks.text: Where are Functions Used in DSA?
In DSA, functions are used to implement algorithms and solve problems in a structured and reusable way.

items: Implement algorithms like searching and sorting.
Operate on data structures like arrays, linked lists, trees, and graphs.
Make code clean and easy to understand.

cards.back:
• Avoids writing the same code again and again.

• Accepts input (parameters) and gives output.
• Finding and fixing errors become easier.
